ranges.note: Two independently checked records concern the approximate Neolithic occupation phase at Koorkula Valgjarv and the first excavated settlement phase at Zurich Parkhaus Opera. The author made 47 queries across all nine working regions and retained 13 withheld or deferred tracks. Both retained records concern Europe; the other regions remain research gaps. Full ranges of 3300-3200 cal BC and 3234-3226 BC remain intact, without annual activity, continuous occupation or coverage of later years inferred from their endpoints. The reviewer confirmed both historical payloads and both substantive source records; two earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Richly furnished burials mark an elite cemetery at Fanshan; Yamnaya communities expand across the Eurasian steppe.

Seven independently checked records concern Newgrange, the approximate foundation of Shahr-i Sokhta, monumental buildings at Uruk, shell-rich deposits at Ru Diep, occupation onset at Upanca, royal imagery at Nag el-Hamdulab and beads in a Kara-depe burial. Full approximate dates, contextual horizons, individual samples and occupation intervals remain distinct. Ru Diep and Upanca keep full ranges extending beyond this century; these establish neither activity in every year nor researched coverage of later centuries. Searches covered nine regions, but sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Oceania and many other areas have no retained event. Upanca retains earlier independently read table evidence; the follow-up access limitation and unverified author retrieval assertions remain explicit in the research note. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Orkney's settlements develop into large mounds.

Six independently checked records concern Egyptian political unification, the Stenness henge, high dams at Liangzhu, the approximate start of the Thach Lac sequence, early weighing objects, and a qualified cattle-husbandry interpretation north of the Black Sea. These are approximate archaeological attestations, constructions or processes; no strict single-calendar-year occurrence is established. Full date intervals, competing chronologies and later endpoints remain in single records. Their spans establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. The Americas, Oceania, South Asia, much of Africa and other regions remain gaps. Empty years are research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Uruk settlements on the Middle Euphrates come to an end.

Six independently checked records concern a brewery at Abydos, the low dams and main city construction at Liangzhu, Stonehenge ditch and banks, a specific Valdivia stone figure, and one burial at Kerma. Full approximate dates and construction intervals remain qualified. Kerma retains a provisional prose estimate alongside the chronology table question mark; settlement samples do not date the grave. Caral, Nausharo, Kot Diji-Amri contacts, aggregated Afanasievo burials and access-limited Kobeba remain withheld. South Asia, Southeast Asia, Oceania, the steppe and much of Africa and the Americas remain gaps. Long intervals establish no occurrence in every year or researched coverage of later centuries. Empty years are research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Pre-Kerma residents occupy a settlement with possible defences.

Five independently checked records concern engraved stones deposited at Vasagard, Dholavira wall reinforcement, a particular Sumerian mace head, a qualified dietary interpretation at Narensu, and grave M118 at Liangwangcheng. Approximate dates, construction periods, object intervals and grave-phase dates remain distinct. Ashqelon abandonment is withheld because the published slash date does not establish the chosen continuous interval. No exact annual occurrence or first cultivation is established. Sub-Saharan Africa, the Americas, Southeast Asia, Oceania and most other areas remain gaps. Full intervals extending beyond this block establish no researched coverage of later centuries. Empty years remain research gaps.

Nine independently checked records concern two Ness of Brodgar building episodes, tentative Harappa perimeter walls, an inscribed Harappa rim sherd, a Linjia tin-bronze knife, three individually dated museum artifacts and initial construction of the Callacpuma circular plaza. Approximate dates and full archaeological or object ranges remain qualified; no exact annual occurrence, manufacturing locality or invented inscription reading is established. Al-Ghoryeen S3 is withheld because its slash date does not explicitly support the proposed continuous interval. The steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Later range endpoints do not establish researched coverage of subsequent centuries. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Vinelz pottery incorporates Corded Ware elements.

Four independently checked historical records concern inferred winter millet foddering at Dali, mixed crop cultivation at Baodun, abandonment of older Kalibangan and covered storage pits on Sai. Approximate site dates, interpretive causes and full occupation ranges remain qualified. Baodun retains 2700-2000 BC and its earlier published 2700-2100 BC alternative; neither implies cultivation in every year or researched coverage of later centuries. Europe, sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, the Americas, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Prior author retrieval dates retain their separately unverified provenance status; the reviewer confirmed all four historical payloads and five substantive source metadata records. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Open grazing landscapes spread in Thy; Khasekhemwy builds a royal cult enclosure at Abydos.

Two independently checked records from the English BC2600 supplement concern the planned urban culture of Mohenjo Daro and Harappa (c. 2600–1900 BC) and Intercultural Style chlorite vessels from southern Iran and the Gulf region (c. 2600–2250 BC). Each cites one Key Events entry of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History; the research read the page text only. Both ranges extend beyond this century and establish neither activity in every year nor researched coverage of later centuries. The cited Egypt page gives no separate date for the Giza pyramids, so no Egyptian record was added. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Nine independently checked records concern the central Stonehenge settings, the approximate creation of ancient Kerma, an Indus jar, a Shijiahe ornament, an attained settlement state at Real Alto, Silbury Hill construction, the probable millet diet of one Aigyrzhal individual, a Sahure statue and Eannatum's victory stele. All nine working regions were searched; Southeast Asia, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Approximate estimates, complete object and sample intervals, and commemorative claims remain distinct. The Aigyrzhal main article supports the event independently; its visually unverified supplement is withheld. Full ranges beyond the century establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Early Beaker graves mark a change in British burial practices.

The original two records concern a rounded room at La Galgada and the funerary texts in Unas's pyramid. Their qualified estimates and competing chronologies remain unchanged. The original search covered nine working regions through 63 queries; the jade object and Ebla palace fire remain withheld after access limitations. A separately reviewed Mesopotamian supplement adds Urukagina's reform inscription and Lugalzagesi's attack on Lagash, bringing the window to four records. Museum object dates, collective archival contexts, alternative reign chronologies and sediment ages remain distinct. Royal claims do not establish universal implementation, and deliberate flooding remains a hypothesis. Seven regions still lack a retained event; empty years and many areas remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Ross Island supplies copper to Ireland and Britain.

Three independently source-checked records concern the Enheduanna disc, the approximate emergence of Shimao as a political centre and Naram-Sin's victory stele. Competing reign chronologies and approximate object dates remain explicit; no exact foundation, battle or carving year is inferred. The author searched all nine working regions through 49 queries, retaining two Mesopotamian records and one East Asian record. Other regions remain gaps. Full date qualifications stay in single records and do not establish activity in each year. Earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: The long occupation of Sannai Maruyama comes to an end.

Three independently checked records concern Akkad’s fragmentation, domestic reuse at Edfu and a qualified climate framework for the Levant. Full competing or approximate intervals remain intact; their endpoints establish no continuous collapse, annual activity, universal drought or researched coverage of later centuries. The author made 30 discovery queries across nine working regions; all retained events concern the Middle East and North Africa, leaving the other eight regions as gaps. Tell Leilan and three object-based event selections remain withheld. Four earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Stone fortifications defend La Bastida; Utuhegal defeats the Gutians.

Eight independently source-checked records concern Dholavira infrastructure decline, Taosi urban enclosure, fortified Sintashta settlements, two Shulgi episodes, Mentuhotep II’s complex and reunification of Egypt, and Ur’s fall. The author logged 32 discovery queries across nine working regions; five retained events concern the Middle East and North Africa, with one each in East Asia, South Asia and the steppe and Central Asia. The other five regions remain gaps. Full phases, reign bounds and competing chronologies remain distinct; Sintashta placement is framework-dependent and Ur’s alternative dynasty endpoint does not independently date a conquest. Public summary, abstract and preview limits remain explicit. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Indus sealing traditions are adapted in Gulf trade.

Sixteen independently checked records cover late Taosi destruction, Khok Phanom Di settlement, Malia palace construction, Gulf settlement changes, Egyptian campaigns and building programmes, Assyrian trade and four distinct Nippur or Isin developments. Full archaeological phases and competing reign chronologies remain intact. Bologna's earlier successful reading and its later access denial are recorded separately. Leubingen remains withheld because its scientific dating evidence was not accessible. Searches covered nine working regions; the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Oceania and the steppe and Central Asia have no retained event. Empty years remain research gaps, and long intervals establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later centuries. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Wooden beds enter Kerma's burial practices.

Ten independently checked records concern Indus settlement changes, Man Bac burial practices, local cacao use, Egyptian urban, military and funerary projects, two attributed Babylonian developments, Xinzhai fortification and Sobekneferu. Bush Barrow remains withheld pending assessment of a referenced chronological reinterpretation. Full phases, Egyptian reign alternatives and separate Xinzhai models remain explicit; manuscript edition and public-abstract reading limits are retained. Searches covered nine macroregions, with Oceania and the steppe and Central Asia among the remaining gaps. Empty years remain research gaps. Intervals extending beyond this block establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later centuries. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: A palace is built at Phaistos; Monumental tombs are built at Kerma.

Sixteen independently checked records concern Malia construction, Gajiganna pastoral occupation, Pampa de las Llamas–Moxeke, Erlitou expansion, Piklihal cereals, interpreted pig management at An Son and ten Mesopotamian political or legal developments. All nine regions were searched; Oceania and the steppe and Central Asia remain gaps. Exact source corrections clarify Erlitou phase models and the An Son interpretation; Gajiganna describes culture rather than a dated migration. Numeric dates and alternatives remain unchanged. Only the traditional Erlitou framework places the phase onset in this century. Full archaeological intervals and competing chronologies establish neither annual occurrence nor researched coverage of adjacent centuries. Earlier retrieval assertions remain separately unverified; empty years remain gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Anitta reports returning Nesha's cult image.

Six independently checked records concern Malia destruction, Hiregudda stone-tool production, Zincirli destruction, Mycenae Grave Circle B, Hyksos rule and interpreted early chicken keeping at Ban Non Wat. All nine regions were searched; sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, the Americas, Oceania and the steppe and Central Asia remain gaps. Poverty Point is withheld after source403 and Karnab after an unsupported numeric endpoint. Zincirli retains exact temporal attribution to a probable reign, separate model ranges and probability qualifications. Other full archaeological intervals, possible interruptions and chronology alternatives remain intact. Long ranges establish neither annual occurrence nor researched coverage of adjacent centuries. Earlier retrieval assertions remain separately unverified; empty years remain gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Hattusili establishes his royal seat at Hattusa; Builders construct an earthen ballcourt at Paso de la Amada.

Five independently checked records from the English BC1600 supplement concern boat images in Scandinavian art, the adoption of bronze in Scandinavia and the Baltic, Shang rule in northern China, Ahmose I's reunification of Egypt and Kerma's loss of Lower Nubia. Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. The Shaft Graves at Mycenae were withheld because the catalog's Grave Circle B record covers them; further entries from Mesoamerica, Lipari and Scandinavia were left for a later pass. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Seven independently checked records concern more sedentary herding near Lake Chad, the broad Kent and San Lorenzo developments, Hatshepsut’s Punt expedition and temple, the disputed Megiddo battle and widespread destruction on Crete. Full approximate intervals remain intact. Megiddo retains the museum’s 1457 BC date and Derstine’s 1468 proposal; the rejected 1482 date remains historical context only. Yale’s public caption supports the Punt year; the full chapter was not accessed. Searches covered nine macroregions, with five represented. East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and Oceania remain gaps. Period intervals establish no activity in every year or researched coverage of adjacent centuries. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Glassworking takes hold in Egypt.

Four independently checked records from the English BC1400 supplement concern the Hittite empire's greatest extent, the Mycenaean palace at Pylos, the first public building at San José Mogote and the ziggurat complex at Chogha Zanbil. Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. The remodelling of the San Lorenzo plateau was withheld because the catalog's San Lorenzo record covers the site; four further candidates were left for a later pass. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Eight candidate records concern the Yin capital move, the Tollense battle, iron-bearing Lahuradeva period III, Talepakemalai stilt houses, the battle of Kadesh, the Mycenae Lion Gate, Merey's attack on Egypt and the Merneptah stele. The original source review returned seven PASS and three HOLD; the narrower Kadesh location requires final candidate review. The treaty and final Mycenae wall phase remain held. All nine working regions were searched, but the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, the steppe and Central Asia have no newly retained record. Represented regions also remain incomplete. Full uncertain dates and intervals remain intact; later endpoints imply neither annual occurrence nor researched coverage of later years. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Glassmakers produce raw glass at Qantir.

Eight independently source-checked records concern Pylos and Thebes palace destructions, the Hallur iron-bearing transition, pearl millet in the Gajiganna sequence, Chavin de Huantar, Ramesses III and the Sea Peoples, the Deir el-Medina work stoppage and the Kassite dynasty collapse. Source review returned eight event PASS and ten source PASS verdicts; the candidate expands only the Hallur locator. All nine working regions were searched, but East Asia, Southeast Asia, Oceania, the steppe and Central Asia have no newly retained record. Represented regions also remain incomplete. Full approximate dates, calibrated evidence, alternative chronologies and intervals remain intact; later endpoints imply neither annual occurrence nor researched coverage of later years. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Ugarit suffers extensive destruction.

Six independently checked event records cover selected developments in the Americas, the Middle East and North Africa, Central Asia, East Asia, Europe and Southeast Asia. All nine macroregions were searched; sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia and Oceania have no retained event in this batch. Cerro Blanco, Chap, Protogeometric pottery and Ban Non Wat retain complete intervals; Smendes and the Zhou conquest retain competing dates. The Chap envelope does not establish continuous occupation across 240 years. The Higham 2009 PDF text was read, but screenshot access returned 403, leaving visual table verification unavailable. Ten leads remain held. Empty years remain research gaps, and interval endpoints do not establish researched later years. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Ritidian's residents intensify coastal activity; Zhou suppresses the Wu Geng rebellion.

Seven independently source-checked event records cover selected developments in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the Americas, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and Oceania. Searches also addressed sub-Saharan Africa and the steppe and Central Asia, which have no retained event. All represented regions remain incomplete. Records preserve the full Pirak 1000-800 BC interval and Vilabouly site sequence from circa 1000 BC to AD 700; these bounds establish neither continuous production nor adjacent researched years. Genkai retains differing regional and broad Yayoi period labels. Teouma uses an explicit BC funerary context from a public abstract, not a cemetery foundation or settlement date. Ceibal cooperation remains an attributed interpretation. Lefkandi uses a heyday marker and Sheshonq a qualified campaign date. Accession, Ahiram, Obobogo and other discovery leads remain withheld. Empty years are research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Metalworkers reach a production peak at Timna's Site 34.

Six independently checked records from the English BC0900 supplement concern terraces and rock reliefs at Chalcatzingo, Korean dolmen burials, La Venta's ceremonial layout, the Manchay Bajo flood wall, Ashurnasirpal II's move to Nimrud in 879 BC and the traditional founding of Carthage in 814 BC. Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. The Carthage record keeps the traditional date and is marked uncertain. Chavín de Huántar's pilgrimage phase was withheld because the catalog's Chavín record covers the site. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Eight independently source-checked records concern Nok ironworking, increased iron objects at Narhan, Cuicuilco construction, Ban Non Wat bronze casting, the traditional first recorded Olympic victor, Western Zhou collapse, a NASA-attributed Assyrian eclipse record and the capture of Lachish. Searches cover all nine macroregions; the steppe and Central Asia and Oceania have no retained event. All regions remain incomplete. Full archaeological ranges and uncertain boundaries remain intact, including Nok 800-400 BC and Cuicuilco 800-150 BC. They establish neither continuous annual activity nor researched coverage of adjacent centuries. Li Feng is limited to the public Summary; the supported event does not imply access to the full chapter. Empty years remain research gaps.

Seven independently source-checked records concern La Venta Stela 3, the destruction of Babylon, the sack of Thebes, Psamtik I in southern Egypt, Chengpu, the traditional date of Draco's homicide law and the destruction of Nineveh. All nine macroregions were searched; sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the steppe and Central Asia and Oceania have no retained event. Coverage remains partial. Late-century Lydian coinage and Arzhan 2 were held after source review because a broad century search frame is not a source-supported numeric event interval. La Venta retains 700-600 BC without extending researched coverage into the next century; Thebes retains 664 or 663 BC, Chengpu its attributed full converted date, and Draco 621/620 BC distinct from the later surviving republication. Babylon support is abstract-only. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Esarhaddon binds oath-takers to his chosen successor; Sennacherib builds a stone aqueduct at Jerwan.

Seven independently checked records from the English BC0600 supplement concern the ceremonial complex at Chiripá, a gold-crown burial at Kuntur Wasi, Milesian colonies on the northern Black Sea, the Scythian Animal Style, the earliest recorded Zapotec date, Cyrus II's founding of the Achaemenid empire (c. 559–530 BC) and the Battle of Aleria. Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. Emporion was withheld until a second source can check its placement; two further candidates were left for a later pass. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Thirty-two source-checked event records concern selected developments in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Searches addressed all nine macroregions; sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, the steppe and Central Asia and Oceania have no retained event. All regions remain incomplete. Two Himera events and their sole source are withheld after the independent reviewer encountered 403. Material corrections were separately checked; editorial importance ranks follow the project scale. Full alternatives remain, including Sparta 469-463 BC, Xerxes succession 465/464, Oresteia 459/458, Egypt 455-454 and Four Hundred 411/410. Approximate Ban Non Wat 420 is distinguished from the full Iron Age 1 phase 420-150. Dates do not imply annual activity, exhaustive coverage or researched adjacent centuries. Empty years remain gaps. English-first supplements add 3 independently checked records: Persepolis records silver payments against rations; Marquis Yi is buried with a large musical assemblage; Elephantine's priests seek support to rebuild their temple.

Thirty independently source-checked records concern selected political, military, cultural and technological developments in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, South Asia, East Asia and Southeast Asia. Searches attempted all nine macroregions; the Americas and Oceania have no retained event. Mediterranean warfare dominates and all regions remain incomplete. The Egypt reconquest in 343/342 event is held because its alternative chronology was access-limited in independent review. Seven bibliographic corrections do not change any retained historical event or numeric date. Full intervals and alternatives remain, including Khao Sam Kaeo 400–101, King's Peace 387–386, Shang Yang 359/356, Alexandria 332–331 and Chandragupta–Seleucus 305–303. Public abstracts and summaries are not represented as full-text access. Full event intervals do not extend researched coverage beyond 400–301 BC. Empty years remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: The Mausoleum rises at Halicarnassus.

30 independently checked event records cover selected developments in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. All nine macroregions were searched; Oceania has no retained event. Mediterranean warfare dominates and many regions, social history and environmental history remain gaps. Kalinga retains approximately 261 or 260 BC; Raphia claims only the battle year 217 BC, with June attributed to the preceding march. Full archaeological and political intervals remain single records and do not extend researched coverage. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Ashoka's edict at Sopara calls for ethical conduct; Priests at Canopus decree an additional festival day.

Thirty-six independently source-reviewed event candidates concern 200–101 BC, with 33 sources and full alternative or extended date ranges retained. The original source review returned 32 PASS and four CORRECTION event verdicts; the candidate applies twelve documented field replacements. Research covered all nine working macroregions, but the retained sample is concentrated in Mediterranean and East Asian political history. Oceania has no retained event; South Asia, Africa, the Americas and Central Asia remain unevenly represented. Public abstracts, publisher descriptions and previews support only the passages actually read. The nine-region search log does not reconstruct missing early query strings. Empty years remain research gaps. Long ranges do not establish coverage of later years. English-first supplements add 1 independently checked record: Silk manuscripts are buried at Mawangdui.

Twenty-seven independently source-reviewed event candidates concern 100-1 BC, retaining 23 sources, full chronological alternatives and intervals. Eight whole events were withheld after independent source-access limitations; eight retained importance values follow exact reviewer replacements. Discovery comprised 53 queries across all nine working macroregions. The retained selection is Roman-heavy, with gaps in South and Central Asia, North and South America and Oceania. Archaeological intervals, traditional foundation dates, inscribed dates and calendar correlations remain qualified. Empty years remain research gaps. Intervals extending into AD years do not establish researched coverage of those years. English-first supplements add 3 independently checked records: Glassworkers develop glassblowing; A merchant ship sinks off Antikythera; Juba II becomes king of Mauretania.

Twenty-six independently checked records concern Rome and its frontiers, Han succession, the Trung sisters and Ma Yuan, Kush, Aksum, Indian Ocean contacts, Tamil literature, Teotihuacan, Monte Alban and the chronicle-attributed Na embassy. All nine regions were searched; Oceania remains a gap and Europe is overrepresented. Four Iranica-dependent events are withheld after403, including Kujula with an unsupported numeric search interval. Fukuoka was separately read after an initial timeout. All retained event and source fields remain unchanged. Broad literary and archaeological periods, the disputed29–34 crucifixion interval, Ma Yuan42–44 and Boudica60/61 remain explicit. Full intervals establish neither annual occurrence nor researched coverage of later centuries. Empty years remain gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Rome builds the Aqua Claudia; Alexandria's Jews face persecution and expulsion.

Twenty-seven independently checked records cover Roman political and military developments, maritime contacts, scientific and technical works, Chinese court changes and Buddhist translations, and Teotihuacan civic rebuilding. Four other candidates remain withheld, two for unresolved complete chronology and two for standalone-event significance. Full intervals and attributed chronologies remain explicit, including AD 101–200 and Kanishka 127/128. Searches covered nine regions; sub-Saharan Africa and Oceania have no retained event, and represented regions remain incomplete. Empty years remain research gaps, and later interval endpoints establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later centuries. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Palmyra's council publishes revised tax rules; The Xiping Stone Classics are prepared in Luoyang.

The original AD200 review retained 17 events and 16 sources after 35 discovery queries across nine regions. A separately reviewed supplement adds two European events and three sources, bringing the window to 19 events. Decius's death retains the sources' May versus early June chronology. Four regions still have no retained event; the twelve original withheld candidates remain withheld. Partial coverage does not establish an event for every year. English-first supplements add 4 independently checked records: Bambata pottery spreads into southeastern Africa; Cao Pi takes the Eastern Han throne; Ardashir establishes the Sasanian dynasty; Wu sends Zhu Ying and Kang Tai to Funan.

Twenty-nine independently source-checked records cover selected events in Europe, East Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Europe has nine records and East Asia eight; Roman imperial and ecclesiastical history dominates. Southeast Asia and Oceania have no retained event. The author logged 21 discovery queries across nine working regions. The Nasca bowl, Sri Lankan tooth-relic account, Pachomios baptism and My Son remain withheld. Puranas retain the full AD301-400 interval, and conflicting source dates remain explicit. Full intervals establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. Empty years and regions remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Royal pyramid burials at Meroe come to an end; The Adosada platform covers Teotihuacan's Feathered Serpent Pyramid façade.

Six independently checked records from the English AD400 supplement concern the Roman departure from Britain (410), the Vandal invasion of North Africa (429), the Egyptian church's rejection of the Council of Chalcedon (451), Goguryeo's capture of Hanseong (475), the Northern Wei move to Luoyang (494) and the conversion of Clovis I (496). Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. Hypatia's death was withheld because the entry gives one sentence only; four further candidates were left for a later pass. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Nineteen independently checked records cover selected events in Europe, East Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Europe has nine records and East Asia five; the remaining represented regions have one each. The Middle East and North Africa and Oceania have no retained event. Rosalila is withheld because its dedication date and source metadata remain unestablished. Exact corrections preserve complete date intervals, source attribution and editorial importance limits. Earlier author retrieval assertions remain unverified. Empty years and regions remain research gaps.

Thirteen independently checked records from the English AD600 supplement concern Hōryūji, the founding of the Tang dynasty (618), the Sutton Hoo ship burial, Xuanzang's journey to India (629–645), the Arab conquest of Egypt (639–642), the battle of Nahavand (642), the Taika Reform (646), the burning of central Teotihuacan, the Synod of Whitby (664), the fall of Goguryeo (668), 'Uqba ibn Nafi' and Kairouan (670), Silla's unification of Korea (676) and the founding of Barhae (698). Each cites one Key Events entry of the Met's Heilbrunn Timeline. The Teotihuacan record is marked uncertain. Seven further candidates were left for a later pass. Other regions and empty years remain research gaps.

Thirty-four independently checked events cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event. Europe has ten records; African coverage is limited to a broadly dated Wanar object, American coverage to Copan and Quirigua, and Southeast Asian coverage to Java. Full intervals and date qualifications remain intact. Two unsupported records are withheld, and earlier author retrieval assertions remain unestablished. Empty years and regions remain research gaps. English-first supplements add 4 independently checked records: Japan permits permanent possession of newly reclaimed rice fields; The Tang court promulgates the two-tax system; Bilge Kagan raises a memorial to Kül Tigin; Sanjaya commemorates a linga dedication at Canggal.

44 independently checked event records cover parts of Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event. Japan and court/religious history are overrepresented; much of Africa, maritime Southeast Asia, northern South Asia, the Americas and other regions need further work. Ife (circa 800–1000) and Igbo-Ukwu (disputed ninth- and tenth-century dates, numeric span 800–999) are single uncertain records whose spans cross the batch boundary. Their presence does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred. English-first supplements add 3 independently checked records: Builders construct linked water reservoirs at Kairouan; Foguang Temple's East Hall is rebuilt; Al-Mutawakkil orders the Rawda nilometer built.

44 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, southern Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas including Greenland. Oceania and Japan have no retained event; sub-Saharan Africa has only Schroda. Northern and eastern South Asia, maritime Southeast Asia, much of Africa and the Americas, and other regions need further research. Shanga and the proposed Kokinshu completion event are withheld because their submitted dates remain unresolved. Tula retains its full circa 900–1150 phase as one record; this does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Gwangjong orders a review of enslaved people's status; Gwangjong introduces civil service examinations in Goryeo.

45 independently checked events cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, southern Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event; sub-Saharan Africa has only the approximate K2 phase. Iberia, Scandinavia beyond Cnut, Egyptian and South Arabian politics, western and central steppe, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, the Philippines, much of Africa and the Americas require more research. Shanga and the proposed Ghana1076 conquest remain withheld. K2 retains its full approximate 1000–1220 phase once; that endpoint does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred. English-first supplements add 3 independently checked records: Song authorities take over jiaozi issuance in Sichuan; Airlangga records support for flood-control works at Kamalagyan; Tamil merchants record a guild meeting at Barus.

56 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and the Caucasus, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Americas including Greenland, and Oceania. Oceania has only Nan Madol; sub-Saharan Africa has Timbuktu, Maryam Nazret and Soso. China and Japan dominate East Asia. Most African regions, the Andes and Caribbean, much of South Asia and maritime Southeast Asia remain gaps. Goryeo1170, Nalanda1193 and proposed exact Oceanian arrivals are withheld; other candidates such as Lalibela remain outside this batch. Maryam Nazret1101–1200, Nan Madol1180–1200 and Cliff Palace1190–1280 retain their complete uncertain or phased intervals once. Their endpoints do not establish researched later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred. English-first supplements add 2 independently checked records: Ali ibn Yusuf expands the al-Qarawiyyin mosque; Nur al-Din builds a hospital in Damascus.
